one_liner: MIT C++ SVG/Lottie vector engine; its CPU renderer averaged 2.9x Skia raster fps on 5k-shape scenes (4 threads vs 1).
what_it_does: ThorVG is a retained-mode 2D vector graphics engine. You build tvg::Shape, Scene, Picture and Text paints, add them to a canvas (SwCanvas over a caller-supplied 32-bit ARGB/ABGR buffer, or GlCanvas/WgCanvas for OpenGL and WebGPU), and call update(), draw() and sync() per frame. It loads SVG (Tiny profile), Lottie (with optional expressions), TTF/OTF, PNG, JPEG and WebP, and supports gradients, dashing, trim paths, masking, blend modes and effects. The API is its own C++ API with an optional C binding, so it is not a drop-in for Skia's immediate-mode SkCanvas.
how_it_is_fast: Per-shape preparation (outline transform, stroking and scan conversion into RLE coverage spans, using a rasterizer derived from FreeType's anti-aliased 'gray' rasterizer) runs as tasks on a worker pool sized by tvg::Initializer::init(n), while the calling thread composites the spans with NEON or AVX2 span blenders. Retained shapes are re-prepared only when their path, transform or colour flags change. Two quality shortcuts save work: axis-aligned unclipped rectangles take a 'fast track' that skips scan conversion and fills a pixel-rounded box without anti-aliasing, and fills under an opaque stroke at least 2 px wide are scan-converted without anti-aliasing. Optional OpenMP row-parallel loops (image scaling, premultiply) and dirty-region partial rendering (SmartRender) add further gains in some scenes.
when_to_use: Lottie playback or SVG icon/UI rendering on the CPU in a C++ app on embedded, mobile or desktop targets, where a core of about 170KB and no mandatory dependencies matter (README lists LVGL, an Espressif ESP-IDF component, Godot, Tizen and Canva iOS as users).

Frames with thousands of retained geometric shapes that move every frame and spare cores to run the worker pool: the README chart gives 3.6x on rotated rectangles and 3.7x on circles over single-threaded Skia v148 raster on an Apple M2 Pro, both anti-aliased on both sides, with ThorVG on 4 worker threads.
Mostly static UIs where only small regions change, since SmartRender partial rendering repaints only dirty regions (the benchmark turns it off, so this gain is not in the chart).
Projects that want one scene-graph API across CPU, OpenGL/ES, WebGL and WebGPU backends, including WebAssembly builds.
when_not_to_use: Image- or gradient-heavy content: the chart shows parity with Skia for PNG images (6.4 vs 6.0 fps), rotated images (4.4 vs 4.4) and linear/radial gradients (1.1x and 1.2x), so switching buys little there.

Single-core or core-limited deployments: the published 2.9x mean pits ThorVG with 4 worker threads (and OpenMP if linked) against single-threaded Skia raster, and no single-threaded ThorVG figure is published.

When you need exact anti-aliased edges on axis-aligned rectangles at fractional coordinates or on fills under thick opaque strokes: the fast track snaps such rectangles to whole pixels, and a TODO in _axisAlignedRect admits it hurts smooth rectangle movement.

When you want the fastest CPU rasterizer: Blend2D and Vello CPU have independent thesis measurements against Skia, ThorVG has none, and in discussion #1815 (December 2023) the maintainer said accurate data including Blend2D was still needed.
Full SVG 1.1/2 documents (only the SVG Tiny subset; no SVG animation, interactivity or multimedia), PDF output, or Skia's breadth in text shaping and colour management.

integration.form: shared lib by default via meson (static with -Ddefault_library=static); packaged in vcpkg, Conan, Homebrew, Debian, Fedora, MSYS2 and others
integration.dependencies: none required; optional OpenMP for the CPU engine (meson option extra=openmp is on by default), libpng/libjpeg-turbo/libwebp for external image loaders (built-in static loaders exist), OpenGL 3.3/ES 3.0 or wgpu-native v29 for the GPU backends
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (meson default cpp_std=c++14), meson and ninja; GCC/Clang builds use -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti
integration.platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, web (WASM), Tizen and RTOS/ESP32 per README; CPU SIMD is AVX2 on x86/x86-64 and NEON on ARM/AArch64 (meson simd option, on by default), with a scalar C fallback
integration.thread_safety: Worker count is fixed by the first successful tvg::Initializer::init(n) (0 means main thread only); update() and draw() may run asynchronously and sync() must follow draw(). Concurrent use of one canvas from several threads is not documented.

gotchas: Axis-aligned, unclipped rectangles are filled as pixel-rounded boxes without anti-aliasing (tvgSwShape.cpp _axisAlignedRect, tvgSwUtil.cpp utilBBox, tvgSwRaster.cpp _rasterRect), and fills under an opaque stroke of 2 px or more are scan-converted aliased (SwShapeTask::antialiasing). Output therefore differs from Skia or Blend2D on such shapes, and slowly moving rectangles step in whole pixels.

SwCanvas::gen() with the default option turns on SmartRender partial rendering, which has an open 'cpu: partial rendering bug' (#4751) and, per the README, can add overhead when nearly everything changes each frame; pass EngineOption::None for full redraws, as the benchmark does. EngineOption::Aliased (turn AA off everywhere) is marked experimental.

With OpenMP built in (the default meson option), the first SwRenderer calls omp_set_num_threads(threads), which also changes the default team size for the host program's own OpenMP regions on that thread.
The scan converter is derived from FreeType code and tvgSwRle.cpp carries the FreeType Project License text, which asks for a FreeType credit in your documentation in addition to the MIT notice.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ThorVG over Blend2D, Vello CPU or AGG when you need SVG and Lottie loading, text, a retained scene graph and optional GPU backends in one small C++14 library for embedded or mobile targets; pick Blend2D when raw single-threaded CPU fill speed is the goal (independent thesis data, about 4x Skia), and LunaSVG when you only rasterize static SVG files.
verified_claims_summary: First-party chart from ThorVG's own public harness (thorvg/thorvg.benchmark): 5,000 shapes per frame at 2560x1440 on an Apple M2 Pro (macOS 26), ThorVG v1.1 with 4 worker threads against Skia v148 from vcpkg drawing single-threaded into a raster surface, frame time including clear and SDL_UpdateWindowSurface; per-test ratios run from 1.0x (rotated images) to 5.6x (rotated rects plus stroke), and the headline 2.9x is their arithmetic mean. No compiler or Skia build flags are named, and no independent measurement exists.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-03, release v1.1.2 on 18 September 2026, about 1.9k stars, dev version 1.2.0 in meson.build) under MIT with FreeType-licensed portions, so it is copyable and widely packaged.
measurement_notes: Harness code read (benchmark_runner.hpp, cli_parser.hpp, tvg_sdl_example.hpp, skia_sdl_example.hpp, rect/strokerect/circle/image benches) plus ThorVG's cpu_engine sources. Both engines clear the frame, draw the same seeded shapes with the same per-frame transforms (scale 0.9-1.1, translation, optional rotation) and present through SDL_UpdateWindowSurface, timed with high_resolution_clock over 1000 frames after 120 warm-up frames; ThorVG partial rendering is disabled (EngineOption::None). Two asymmetries favour ThorVG. (1) Threads: CliOptions.threads defaults to 4 (the --help text still says max), so ThorVG prepares shapes on 4 workers while Skia draws on one thread; ThorVG's compositing itself stays on the calling thread, but with the default meson build (extra=openmp, and the harness README installs libomp) scaled-image loops are also OpenMP row-parallel. (2) Unequal output: every Skia paint sets setAntiAlias(true), but ThorVG's fast track fills the Rects test's axis-aligned rectangles (no rotation in the default scene) as pixel-rounded boxes without AA, and in both Rects+Stroke tests the 3 px white opaque stroke (2.7-3.3 px after scaling) disables AA on the fill beneath it. So the 4.4x, 4.0x and 5.6x rows compare less work on the ThorVG side; the like-for-like AA rows are Rotated Rects 3.6x and Circles 3.7x, which still carry the 4-threads-versus-1 asymmetry, while images and gradients are at parity even with that advantage. The Stroke row predates the 2026-09-21 designer-strokes workload, as the verifier noted. Not a correctness bug in ThorVG (the shortcuts are deliberate design), but a measurement flaw worth a shortcoming; tier C stands.
